entry.title: GTC Berlin: Vera Rubin in a shipping container, while neocloud financing worries dominate the floor (6 minute read)
entry.content:
Nvidia's GTC Berlin centered on the DSX POD, a factory-built Vera Rubin NVL72 system in a shipping container that cuts delivery to deployment from months to days, plus OpenShell agent sandboxing and the Agile ONE SN humanoid on Jetson Thor. Nvidia said it has invested nearly $10 billion in Europe.

entry.title: Musk says SpaceX closed $40B of GPU debt for chips arriving in Q1 and Q2 (2 minute read)
entry.content:
Elon Musk says SpaceX closed its $40 billion of callable debt for GPUs, with the chips arriving in Q1 and Q2 and "not a major factor this quarter." He credits investment-grade status and Starlink and launch revenue for keeping credit open. SpaceX guided Q4 capex to $35 to $40 billion. It is bringing roughly 200,000 GB300s online monthly through year-end before shifting to Vera Rubin. The company reported 1.7 GW of installed GPU nameplate capacity at September 30.

entry.title: Warhound raises $200M at a $1.2B valuation to engineer military dogs and outfit them with Anduril sensor gear (4 minute read)
entry.content:
Warhound is a startup founded by Colossal's Ben Lamm and Anduril's Palmer Luckey that plans to gene-edit Belgian Malinois and German Shepherd cell lines into working dogs with better health, speed, and smell. Anduril will supply the hardware: protective vests with data sensors that feed handlers, plus goggles. Viagen will clone the first batch, with births expected early next year and service within two years. The dogs don't exist yet, and sale prices are undecided.

entry.title: NASA reworks Artemis around Orion's limited propulsion, with Starship pushing it toward the Moon (4 minute read)
entry.content:
NASA turned Artemis III into a roughly two-week Earth-orbit test in summer 2027, where Orion docks with test versions of Blue Moon and Starship. For the 2028 landing on Artemis IV, Starship would dock with Orion in high Earth orbit and perform the trans-lunar injection burn, while Blue Moon meets Orion in low lunar orbit, which cuts its propellant needs. NASA will pick the Artemis IV lander based on Artemis III results.

entry.title: Pt-W alloy tested as a thinner low-n absorber for High-NA EUV photomasks (1 minute read)
entry.content:
Researchers at the Chinese Academy of Sciences, Jilin University, and partner labs evaluated a platinum-tungsten alloy as a low-n absorber for EUV photomasks, studying its film properties and imaging performance. Thinner absorbers matter for High-NA EUV because mask 3D effects degrade imaging as features shrink. Thickness and contrast figures are in the iScience paper published in August.

entry.title: MIT's light-steered swimming robot runs on a hair-thin layer of living muscle (3 minute read)
entry.content:
MIT built a swimming robot from a gum-stick-sized gel frame with two fins, each coated in a muscle layer thinner than a hair and engineered to contract under light. Lighting one fin or both steers it through a maze at about four body lengths per minute. The key fixes were stiff GelMA gel about half a millimeter thick with square-bottomed grooves that align the cells, and light-pulse training to strengthen the muscle. It's the first thin 2D biohybrid swimmer.

entry.title: iFixit's iPhone Duo teardown gives the best foldable repair score so far, but the inner screen is the catch (8 minute read)
entry.content:
iFixit gives the iPhone Duo a provisional 5/10, the best score for a foldable. Both batteries (19.1 Wh total) release with electrically debonded adhesive inside metal shells, the outer display comes off intact, and the logic board is a single layer. The weak spot is the inner screen: a $999 out-of-warranty replacement and a hinge that still crunches with dust.

entry.title: Intel's CTO says tools can only roughly double leading-edge chip output, while AI demand grows 3x a year (50 minute read)
entry.content:
Dwarkesh Patel toured Intel's fabs and interviewed its leaders. CTO Pushkar Ranade said that there are enough tools to roughly double leading-edge output, not 10x. Backside power lets Intel's 14A print with a single High-NA pass, where TSMC would still need double-patterned EUV. Other topics discussed included ruthenium wiring below roughly 20nm pitch, CFET aspect-ratio and heat challenges, hybrid bonding pitches shrinking toward 0.45 microns, and the Terafab partnership.

entry.title: New superconducting chip aims to help tame fusion plasma (5 minute read)
entry.content:
Brookhaven National Laboratory debuted a superconducting chip built with other US Department of Energy facilities and AI hardware startup Great Sky to monitor fusion plasma in real time. The chip runs a neuromorphic neural network meant to spot signs that superhot plasma is about to become unstable. Its backers hope the hardware is fast enough to help control plasma before disruptions form, a prerequisite for practical fusion power.

entry.title: Electric Seagliders Promise Faster Coastal Travel by 2028 (8 minute read)
entry.content:
Regent's Viceroy Seaglider, the largest electric wing-in-ground-effect craft to fly with people aboard, made its maiden flight on September 2, covering 596 meters over 30 seconds at about 10 meters above the water. The 16.8-meter craft carries 12 passengers at up to 290 kph with a 290-kilometer range, and is classified as a maritime vessel under US law, sidestepping the FAA certification limbo facing eVTOLs. Regent has raised more than $340 million, claims a $10 billion order backlog, and plans commercial production at the end of 2027.

entry.content:

The chip packs 46 cores (6 XiangShan Kunminghu V2R2 plus 40 SpacemiT X100) at 2.2-2.4GHz on 12nm with a 120W TDP, supports eight-channel DDR5-4800 and 52 PCIe 5.0 lanes, and scales to two sockets and 92 cores. entry.title: Nvidia Vera's memory system delivers 1.2 TB/s with flat latency, but cross-socket links lag (5 minute read)
entry.content:
Chips and Cheese's teardown of Vera's fabric found a 1024-bit LPDDR5X-9600 interface delivering 1.228 TB/s, with latency staying under 200 ns even as bandwidth load climbs, plus a 164 MB shared L3 and field-serviceable SOCAMM2 modules. NVLink C2C moves up to 780 GB/s between sockets, but cross-socket core-to-core latency is around 660 ns. Vera trails Graviton 5 on socket-level throughput but leads by nearly 20% in DRAM-bound SPEC tests.

entry.title: Why Physical AI Is So Hard To Engineer (13 minute read)
entry.content:
This article presents views from Synopsys, Keysight, Renesas, Arteris, Cadence, and Mixel on how physical AI changes chip design. Engineers must handle unpredictable environments, safety and serviceability, and split designs between devices that can rely on the cloud and those that must run fully locally, such as vehicles. Several speakers frame it as a sensing and imaging problem as much as a compute one.

entry.title: AI hardware design is the easy part, the lossy physical interface is the bottleneck (15 minute read)
entry.content:
AI will soon be superhuman at hardware design, but the digital-to-physical interface is lossy. Building real parts means navigating CNC/CAM translation, tolerance stacking, vendors, and scale, while measuring reality is sparse, slow, expensive, and sometimes qualitative. Demand is expected to shift toward suppliers of machined parts, harnesses, and components, plus better simulation and process-knowledge data.

entry.title: NASA's Roman telescope beats its image-quality spec by nearly 30% after a hair-width mirror nudge (3 minute read)
entry.content:
After moving Roman's secondary mirror by about one-sixteenth the width of a human hair, engineers measured 63 nanometers RMS of optical error in the Wide Field Instrument, nearly 30% better than the 90-nanometer requirement. The camera has 18 detectors, and the same adjustment fixed slight defocus in the Coronagraph Instrument, which still needs testing of its ability to block unwanted light. Roman launched August 30, and both instruments now match or beat predictions.

entry.title: Tesla Roadster pairs underbody suction fans with cold-gas thrusters for grip beyond what tires allow (3 minute read)
entry.content:
The Roadster's floor uses fans and perimeter seals to pull air out from under the car, creating up to 2 g of suction, enough to hold it upside down while stationary, and at speed, front and rear passages open for more flow. Cold-gas thrusters add a second system: ten nozzles fed by compressed air, with all-electric actuators for fast micro-adjustments, which Tesla says push with four to five times the force tires can deliver.

entry.title: Variable frequency drives could free up grid power by cutting motor energy use 40 to 60 percent (5 minute read)
entry.content:
Variable frequency drives adjust motor speed to match demand, cutting a motor's energy use by about 40 to 60 percent. Toyota saved over $700,000 a year after putting them on 200-plus HVAC motors at its Kentucky plant, in a $1.25 million pilot. Cheaper sensors, machine-learning control, and power chips borrowed from EVs and solar inverters have cut costs. ABB claims drives on every motor could cover up to five years of data center load growth.

entry.title: Spin waves coupled to a superconducting circuit create a one-way street for microwave signals (3 minute read)
entry.content:
Argonne and UIUC researchers coupled spin waves in a thin yttrium iron garnet film to a superconducting resonator built directly on top, creating a hybrid mode that propagates one way and could keep return noise from leaking back into qubits. The key materials fix was swapping the usual rare-earth-containing substrate, which absorbs microwaves at low temperatures, for one without rare-earth metals. It's still a proof of concept.

entry.title: Kornia-SLAM: Visual-Inertial Odometry and SLAM in Rust (3 minute read)
entry.content:
Kornia-SLAM is an open-source visual-inertial odometry and spatial mapping library implemented entirely in Rust. It supports monocular, stereo, and RGB-D cameras coupled with inertial measurement units, utilizing factor graph optimization to maintain real-time performance and strict memory safety. This framework gives embedded software teams a reliable, crash-resilient foundation for real-time spatial estimation on compute-limited physical devices.

The architecture allows creators of intelligent physical machines to translate natural language goals into dexterous, real-world manipulation and navigation.

entry.title: Google's Willow chip cuts quantum magic-state errors 40x with cultivation (4 minute read)
entry.content:
Google ran magic state cultivation on its Willow chip, cutting errors about 40x versus uncultivated states and reaching a record 99.99% logical fidelity for T-states. Magic states are a bottleneck because making them could consume up to 95% of a quantum computer's capacity. Cultivation injects a noisy state into a small chip region, then uses coordinated measurements to discard flawed attempts, and Google grafted a distance-3 color code onto a distance-5 surface code. Larger-scale demonstrations are still needed.

entry.title: Ayar Labs and GUC simulate a 3 kW co-packaged optics package, and only liquid cooling holds spec (4 minute read)
entry.content:
Ayar Labs and GUC simulated a 105mm by 140mm package with two XPUs, eight HBM4 stacks, and eight TeraPHY optical engines, offering over 100 Tbps of optical bandwidth at more than 3 kW. A standard air heatsink at 5 to 6 m/s failed spec, while an impingement liquid cold plate at 4.5 L/min kept the optical engines under 100°C. Results use static power assumptions, so dynamic workload simulation is next.

entry.title: Monazite ore could supply EV motor magnet metals, if the thorium waste can be handled (19 minute read)
entry.content:
Monazite ore is 45 to 70 percent rare earths by weight and carries all four elements motor magnets need (neodymium, praseodymium, dysprosium, and terbium), making it a leading path around China's roughly 90 percent market share. The catch is thorium, whose waste must be stored indefinitely. Energy Fuels already produces neodymium-praseodymium oxide plus pilot dysprosium and terbium at its Utah mill, while Saskatchewan's government-backed plant has produced little after six years and over CA$100 million.

entry.content:
